title: Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026
official_summary:
Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026

This act reauthorizes through FY2031 and revises programs that support research and development of drugs and other therapies to address amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (also known as ALS or Lou Gehrig's disease) and other neurodegenerative diseases.

The act reauthorizes

  • grants from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) for scientific research on investigational drugs to prevent or treat ALS for individuals not otherwise eligible for clinical trials,
  • grants from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for research and development of therapies to prevent and treat ALS and other neurodegenerative diseases, and
  • a Public-Private Partnership including the FDA and NIH that supports development and regulatory review of treatments for neurodegenerative diseases. 

Also, the NIH, in considering renewal of its grants, must assess available information on the safety and efficacy of the investigational drugs. It must also require grantees to promptly report serious and unexpected adverse events associated with their investigational drugs.

Additionally, the FDA must publish a plan describing actions it will take over a five-year period to foster development of safe and effective drugs, and facilitate access to investigational drugs, that treat ALS and other rare neurodegenerative diseases. The FDA must also publish a report describing the actions it has taken under the plan.

summary.headline: Extends federal ALS research and drug access programs through 2031 and adds new safety reporting and FDA planning requirements.
summary.what_it_does: The law renews, through fiscal year 2031, NIH grants that study experimental ALS drugs given to patients who cannot join clinical trials, FDA grants for developing ALS and other brain-disease treatments, and an FDA-NIH partnership with private groups. When deciding whether to renew grants, NIH must review safety and effectiveness information, and grant recipients must quickly report serious, unexpected side effects. The FDA must publish a five-year plan to support development of and access to drugs for ALS and other rare neurodegenerative diseases, and later report on what it did.

who_it_affects.how: Programs that may give them access to experimental drugs outside of clinical trials continue through 2031, with added safety reporting.
FDA grants, a public-private partnership, and a new FDA plan aim to support development of treatments for their conditions.

who_it_affects.group: Researchers and organizations receiving NIH ALS grants
who_it_affects.how: They must promptly report serious and unexpected side effects, and NIH will review drug safety and effectiveness before renewing their grants.
They remain eligible for FDA grants and partnership support for ALS and neurodegenerative disease treatments.
The agencies must continue these programs and the FDA must publish a five-year plan and a progress report.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted November 3, 2026; programs are reauthorized through fiscal year 2031.
